name: Ginkgo biloba
short: Trials of clotting measures indicate no higher bleeding risk, but case reports describe bleeding, including intracranial. Interactions with anticoagulant or antiplatelet medicines cannot be ruled out.
text: A meta-analysis of 18 randomised trials (1985 adults) found no significant effect of standardised ginkgo leaf extract on platelet aggregation and no indication of a higher bleeding risk. However, a systematic review of 15 published case reports, 8 of them involving bleeding inside the skull, judged a causal link between ginkgo and bleeding to be possible, although 13 of the reports identified other risk factors for bleeding. A review of placebo-controlled trials found no excess of side effects over placebo, listed minor ones (stomach upset, headache, dizziness, constipation, forceful heartbeat and allergic skin reactions), and stated that interactions with anticoagulant or antiplatelet medicines cannot be ruled out and that, as a general precaution, withdrawing ginkgo two weeks before planned surgery is recommended.
